chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'My zakat becomes due upon me in a specific month. Is it permissible for me to withhold a portion of it, fearing that someone may come to me asking for it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the year passes, then extract it from your wealth, do not mix it with anything, then give it however you wish.'
He (the narrator) said: I said, 'And if I write it down and establish it as correct for me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It will not harm you.'

key_terms.حَالَ الْحَوْلُ: When the year has passed (completion of the lunar year for zakat)

ai.seo_question: When should zakat be paid and can I keep a record of it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural purity of zakat by mandating its immediate separation from general wealth upon the completion of the lunar year (hawl), ensuring it is not commingled with other assets. It further validates the practice of formally recording or establishing the obligation, a detail that highlights the practical administrative flexibility within Shia jurisprudence. The Imam’s permission to distribute 'as you wish' underscores the discretion granted to the payer in selecting recipients, provided the core condition of timely extraction is met.
